title: Practice rules and penalties — Ellery Tax Group
instructions: Ellery Tax Group's CPAs prepare individual returns. Select the most appropriate response to each situation, then compute the penalties for Mia Chen.

exhibits.title: Situations
exhibits.content:
1. A client wants to claim a deduction for which there is **no reasonable basis**, and offers to attach a disclosure statement.
2. A position has a **reasonable basis** but not substantial authority, and isn't a tax shelter item.
3. While preparing a 2025 return, a CPA learns the client didn't file a required 2023 return.
4. A client's 2025 return was filed on **March 1, 2026**; the due date was April 15, 2026. No fraud or substantial omission.
5. An IRS agent properly requests records the CPA holds for a client under examination; the CPA doesn't believe they are privileged.

exhibits.title: Mia Chen
exhibits.content: Mia filed a timely extension for her 2025 return but paid nothing by April 15, 2026. She filed the return and paid the **$20,000** balance on **August 15, 2026**. Ignore interest.

rows.label: 1. No reasonable basis
rows.explanation: A position must have at least a reasonable basis and be disclosed to avoid the §6694(a) penalty; disclosure can't rescue a position with no reasonable basis.

rows.label: 2. Reasonable basis only
rows.explanation: A reasonable-basis position is acceptable if adequately disclosed (for example, on Form 8275).

rows.label: 3. Unfiled prior-year return
options: Promptly advise the client of the noncompliance and its consequences
Notify the IRS of the client's noncompliance
Prepare the 2025 return and say nothing
rows.answer: Promptly advise the client of the noncompliance and its consequences
rows.explanation: Circular 230 §10.21 requires the practitioner to advise the client promptly of the noncompliance and its consequences; there is no duty to notify the IRS.

rows.label: 4. Assessment period ends
rows.explanation: An early return is treated as filed on the due date, so the three-year period runs from April 15, 2026.

rows.label: 5. IRS records request
options: Refuse unless the client consents in writing
Ignore it until a summons is issued
rows.explanation: Circular 230 §10.20: a practitioner must promptly submit records properly requested by the IRS unless believed in good faith to be privileged.

rows.label: Failure-to-file penalty
rows.explanation: The return was filed within the extended due date: **0**.

rows.label: Failure-to-pay penalty
rows.explanation: An extension doesn't extend the time to pay: 0.5% × 4 months × 20,000 = **400**.
